title: bulgarias nuclear plant cut capacity due danubes low water level 2026 08 20
text:
SOFIA, Aug 20 (Reuters) - Bulgaria's sole nuclear power plant said it will cut capacity by about ​12% on Friday due to the Danube ‌river's low water levels.
The Kozloduy Nuclear Power Plant (NPP), which provides around 35% of Bulgaria's electricity needs, operates two ​1,000 MW Soviet-made reactors - Units 5 and 6. ​It said it would cut capacity at ⁠unit 5 by about 120 MW to ensure ​the plant's safe operation.
The decision was taken due ​to the "ongoing unprecedented and critical decrease in the Danube River", the plant said, adding that this was the first time ​in its 52-year operational history that the ​power capacity had to be reduced due to extreme hydrological ‌conditions.
Record ⁠low water levels in Europe's major rivers have reduced electricity output, with nuclear power production in Hungary and hydropower in Serbia falling sharply because of ​the Danube's ​low levels.
Last ⁠week, Romania's sole nuclear power producer Nuclearelectrica (ROSNN.BX)

 shut down its plant completely due ​to the low Danube.
A team set ​up at ⁠Kozloduy in July has implemented necessary procedures to ensure the plant's safe and reliable operation in ⁠the ​event of a prolonged drop in ​river levels, the company said.
